> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0b5588cfc4cafd88ad22526f7fd81cf1256a41db` — the merge of head `9e26304a5c78e9429672ddf864768e7e6500081a` into base `0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0b5588cfc4cafd88ad22526f7fd81cf1256a41db && git checkout 0b5588cfc4cafd88ad22526f7fd81cf1256a41db
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1 9e26304a5c78e9429672ddf864768e7e6500081a && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1 && git merge --no-ff 9e26304a5c78e9429672ddf864768e7e6500081a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9e26304a5c78e9429672ddf864768e7e6500081a`
Local-runs: none

Read-only review of PR #21203 (`Fixes #20701`, line 2 `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; draft; head repo equals base repo; 10 files, +617 / −39) against `main` at the merge base `0d421041d14cfc716e85e9bdd1da3d57d4eb3aa1`. Inputs: card #20701's body and all 34 comments (through the takeover claim 5936863307), the PR body, its file list and net diff, the check-runs on the head, and files read at `origin/main` with `git show` / `git grep`. Every path this PR touches, plus `bulk-write.ts`, `protocol.ts`, `protocol.zod.ts`, `data-engine.zod.ts`, the gate script and the two workflows named below, is byte-identical between the merge base and `origin/main`; the only moved file among those consulted is `rest-server.ts`, one description string far from the import routes. Nothing was built, run or re-run. One attempt to read the red job's log was refused by the proxy, so that job's signature below is its failing STEP from the jobs API, with no first error line.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, named and judged:

1. **`@objectstack/core` published TypeScript surface widens — RIGHT.** `packages/core/src/index.ts` re-exports `./utils/import-runner.js` whole, so `ImportRowResult` (gains optional `droppedFields`, typed `DroppedFieldsEvent[]` from `@objectstack/spec/data`) and `ImportProtocolLike` (its `insertManyData` outcome element gains optional `droppedFields`) are published. Both additions are optional keys: an existing implementor of `insertManyData` still type-checks, an existing reader of `ImportRowResult` is unaffected, and the new outcome type is spelled exactly as the real protocol's own signature at `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:13744`. Additive widening; nothing removed, renamed, narrowed or refused. `createData` / `updateData` stay typed `any` on the interface, as before.

2. **The dry run now carries the engine's per-row drops — RIGHT.** `previewVerdict` already returned the first element of `validateData`'s `results`, the per-row verdict, and `ValidateDataResponseSchema.results[]` declares `droppedFields` since #20921 (`protocol.zod.ts:2146`). The diff spreads `rowDrops(verdict?.droppedFields)` only into the two `ok` arms; a refused dry-run row and a skipped row are untouched. `rowDrops` adds the key only when the report is a non-empty array, so a clean row grows no empty key, matching the describe's "present only when at least one field was dropped".

3. **The commit through `insertManyData` — RIGHT.** `flushPendingCreates` hands `bulkWrite` the buffered rows' `data` objects themselves, `bulkWrite` slices that array without copying, `splitByExisting` pushes the same objects into `toCreate`, and `writeOne` receives the batch element; so a `Map` keyed by the row object and read back through `batch[res.index].data` resolves to the right row. Outcome `k` is `toCreate[k]`'s, and the recovered-outcomes path (`recoverSummaryStale`) keeps that order, so the summary-stale case is attributed per row too (pinned). A row a retry attempt found already committed gets no entry and therefore no key, which the code comment states: that is an omission, never a false report.

4. **The commit through `createData` (the inline path and `bulkWrite`'s per-row degradation) and through `updateData` — RIGHT.** Both responses are one row's; `responseDrops` reads only the key `CreateDataResponseSchema` and `UpdateDataResponseSchema` declare. On the update path the read sits inside the `try`, so a recovered record (summary stale) carries no key rather than a guessed one.

5. **Verbatim copy, no second vocabulary, no reason read — RIGHT, and triage's ⛔ holds** (5906762084, 5910777625: no import-side list of non-writable types; the engine's report is the only source). `rowDrops` copies the array and never inspects `reason`; one core pin drives a reason outside today's enum through unchanged.

6. **The two named absences — RIGHT, and both are stated where a reader looks** (the core header, the spec describe, the changeset). (a) `createManyData` answers a batch-level union whose own docblock says a name there means "at least one row dropped this field" and forbids a per-row reconstruction (`protocol.ts`, the docblock above `:13744`), so those rows carry no key. (b) An `update`-mode preview runs no `readonlyWhen` or primary-key strip, so an upsert row matched to a locked record names nothing on the dry run and `readonly_when` on the commit; pinned as the limit (the pin flips on purpose when the engine closes it). Reach of (a), measured on `origin/main`: the four in-tree `runImport` callers are the two REST routes and `service-automation`'s connector pull, which hand in the real protocol service (it has `insertManyData`), and `plugin-auth`'s admin user import, whose hand-built double deliberately offers no bulk primitive at all, so its rows take the inline `createData` path. No in-tree caller takes the `createManyData`-only path; the absence is a declared limit of the published contract, not a reachable gap today.

7. **Published spec shape `ImportRowResultSchema` — RIGHT: the accept set does not move.** `export.zod.ts` changes a TSDoc block, one describe string and a path in the neighbouring `warnings` bullet (the runner moved to core in PR #21084); no key, type, refinement or default changes. The new describe is true of the runner: a committed row reports what its write made; a dry-run row reports what its preview runs, excluding the update-mode `readonlyWhen` / primary-key strips; absence does not prove nothing was dropped. The old sentence "a dry-run row reports the strips the write would make" would be false for exactly that update-mode cell, so correcting it is owed. `export.test.ts` changes a comment only.

8. **`content/docs/references/api/export.mdx` — RIGHT.** AUTO-GEN, not hand-edited: the three changed `droppedFields` rows are byte-equal to the new describe, and `check:docs` (inside the required `TypeScript Type Check` job) is green on this head, which is the gate that reds on a hand edit or a stale regeneration.

9. **The REST wire — RIGHT, no REST source edit needed.** On `origin/main` the sync route answers `results: summary.results` (`rest-server.ts:9268`), the job worker persists `capImportResults(summary.results)` (`:9459`), which filters and slices rows whole, and the results route returns the stored items; so an `ok` row's new key reaches all three. The new REST pin measures the three at the wire against a real engine (sync dry run and commit, upsert, the async job's results route with `dryRun` true and false), including equality with the create door's and `PATCH`'s own `droppedFields`.

10. **Tests — RIGHT in direction.** The flipped `import-row-report-field-20701.test.ts` cells, which pinned only that both halves succeed, now also assert the reported strip and its reason; the header's "not pinned here" paragraph is replaced accordingly. No pin was weakened.

11. **Not governed.** None of the 10 paths is a governed surface; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green. No ADR surface is touched, and ADR-0087 is not engaged (nothing breaking).

Residues, acceptance notes only, none blocking: the retry-found-existing row's missing key (item 3) is stated in a code comment and covered by the describe's generic "a server or write path that does not produce this report omits the key", but is not named in the changeset; the `readonlyWhen` fork's "revisit B" trigger (the #20922 seat ruling) was measured by the dev against objectui `edfcf5a` with no consumer found, and that reading is the dev's, not re-measured here.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` — RIGHT.** Item 1 above is an additive widening of `@objectstack/core`'s published TypeScript surface, and the served REST import row gains a key that was declared but never produced. Nothing narrows: no accept set shrinks, no key is removed, renamed or refused. The arm is the widening arm, so no BREAKING marker and no ADR-0087 disposition are owed. This is seat answer B on the card (5935693776, open to veto, none recorded through comment 34), consistent with the lane's grading of the same act on #20922.
- **`.changeset/20701-import-row-dropped-fields.md`: `@objectstack/core: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: patch` — RIGHT.** `yes` takes at least `minor` on the package whose surface widens, and core is that package. Spec's change is text only (TSDoc, one describe, and the generated docs page it feeds), with the schema's accept set unchanged: `patch`. `@objectstack/rest` publishes nothing from this diff (two test files only), so no rest changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` does not apply. The changeset body carries the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line, and its claims match the diff: the four reason arms are the engine's enum, the three REST surfaces are pinned, the two absences are the ones in item 6, and the `insertManyData` outcome type is the one in item 1. The gate's level axis accepted it: the `Check Changeset` job's steps "Require a changeset", "Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset" and "Guard against accidental major bumps" are green on this head; its one red step is the deliberate correction below.

#### The deliberate correction: two changesets this PR edits but did not add

`check-empty-changeset` (the `Check Changeset` job's step "Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR") refuses both edits by name. Its source at the merge base (identical on `origin/main`) names the two classes and gives the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class the remedy "do NOT restore it -- say so on the PR and get it confirmed". Both notes are still pending on `origin/main` (neither has been consumed by a release), so each would ship in the same release as this PR.

- **`.changeset/20921-import-row-dropped-fields.md`** — removed sentence: "The key is declared ahead of its producer." Replacement: none (pure removal; the surrounding line is otherwise byte-identical). Judgment: once this PR lands, `runImport` produces `ImportRowResult.droppedFields` and the engine produces `ValidateDataResponse.results[].droppedFields` (#20922), so the key ships alongside its producer and the sentence would be false. The edit is a correction and nothing more. Every other sentence of the note stays true after landing: the schema additions, the engine's reason vocabulary with no second enum, unchanged `ok` / `action` / `valid`, "a server that does not produce the report omits the key" (still true for the two absences in ① item 6), the `warnings` paragraph, the capped-sample paragraph and the exhaustive-consumer paragraph.

- **`.changeset/20922-per-row-dropped-fields.md`** — removed sentence: "The REST import route does not copy the per-row report onto its row results yet." Replacement: none (pure removal; the rest of the line is byte-identical). Judgment: once this PR lands, the import runner the REST import route calls copies the per-row report onto each `ok` row and the route serves it (① item 9), so the sentence would be false. Correction and nothing more. Every other sentence stays true: the per-row answers of `validate` / `validateData` and `insertMany` / `insertManyData`, recorded at the strips, the hook exemption, "a row the write does not complete carries none", the update-mode preview limit (which this PR relies on and names), the unchanged batch-level union, and the `minor` grading in both packages.

- No other pending note is made false by this diff: the three earlier `20701-*` REST notes, `20805-formula-write-strip.md` and `20963-not-null-hint-declared-column.md` were read on `origin/main`, and none states that the import row lacks the drop signal.

The three ride-the-red conditions (SKILL.md), each read on the merge base, which the head carries unchanged:
1. The gate's own source declares the class red by design, with the confirmation remedy quoted above (`scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`).
2. The job has no queue leg: `pr-automation.yml` triggers on `pull_request` only (no `merge_group` anywhere in the file), and `lint.yml`'s unconditional changeset-family step runs the `--self-test` halves only, by its own comment, so the queue's rebuilt generation never runs the real scan.
3. This record is the PR comment that names the gate, the two notes, each removed sentence and why it would be false. Per the landing rules, a same-head contract-review PASS record is the confirmation; nothing further is awaited.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and `open_questions` entry from the two reports on this head's branch (5935656110, 5935832005), the seat answer (5935693776), the release (5936634032) and the takeover claim (5936863307):

- **Open question 1 (round 0): which `Clause-②` line.** Answered by seat answer B; applied in round 1 (commit `ff2ea1c7f1`; the head carries `'@objectstack/core': minor`, the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line and the PR body's line 2). Judged RIGHT in ②. Closed.
- **Deviation: file surface beyond the claim** (spec text, the generated page, a spec test comment, two predecessor changesets). Each edit corrects text the change makes false (① items 7 and 8, the correction subsection), and the takeover claim names all 10 files as the surface. The spec touch owes this at-tier review; this record is it. Closed.
- **Deviation: changeset levels.** Settled with the open question. Closed.
- **Deviation: merges of `origin/main`.** The last, `0d421041d1`, is the merge base of this head; `main` has since moved only on paths outside this diff's files (one `rest-server.ts` description string). The landing-time `merge-tree` is the seat's. Noted.
- **Deviation: harness attribution.** The PR body ends with the session-URL footer and carries no model identifier; the changeset carries none. Closed.
- **Deviations: throwaway probes deleted; worktree cleanup; the body's "Line 2 declares a widening" wording.** Nothing to answer; the file list carries no probe file. Closed.
- **Out-of-scope finding: the update-mode preview fork ("revisit B").** The dev measured no consumer acting on update-row previews or on `ImportRowResult.droppedFields` in objectui; nothing is filed. The limit is pinned and documented. Taken as noted, not escalated.
- **Out-of-scope finding: `createManyData`-only protocols NOT MEASURED.** Measured here on `origin/main` (① item 6): no in-tree caller takes that path. Closed; nothing to file.
- **Release 5936634032: the at-tier review record was refused by a permission layer and never posted.** This record is the re-run on `9e26304a5`, written through the fleet relay.
- **Release 5936634032: the three ride-the-red conditions.** The seat verified two; all three are verified above, the third being this comment.
- **Dispatch ⛔s** (claim 5932483988): no change to the async job's results cap (`capImportResults` untouched; the describe still names the capped, failures-first sample) and no `storage.notNull` judgment in the preview (the preview reads `validateData` only). Both hold.
- Nothing is escalated.

#### Check-runs on the head (read at 2026-10-01T17:31Z)

42 check-runs on `9e26304a5c78e9429672ddf864768e7e6500081a`, all `completed`. The seven required contexts all read `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Also `success`: `Build Docs`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Check PR Size`, `Auto Label`, the four `Type Check ·` jobs, the six `Test Core (n/6)` and three `Dogfood Regression Gate (n/3)` shards, `filter`, and the five PR-automation claim and part-of guards. `skipped`: `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, and one earlier `Auto Label` / `Check PR Size` pair. The only `failure`: `Check Changeset`, twice (job ids 110470696709 and 110471069144, the second triggered by the body edit); in both, the one failing step is "Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR", the step that runs `check-empty-changeset.mjs`, with every other step of that job `success` or `skipped` as designed.
